about: The ledger contract: every event kind in ledger.jsonl, the one script that writes it, and its fields.
Each field's type is string, number or array (a list), or a list of the strings it may be.
Every line has ts (UTC, like 2026-10-22T01:00:00Z), task (T<n>) and event; note (a string) is allowed on every kind, and other fields are allowed.
Lines from strict_from on must meet their kind's fields; earlier lines are legacy and only need ts, task and event.
Legacy lines keep shapes no kind has now: closes by hand with no lists, and plan-ready, which is not a kind, since a planner's report is done and a plan put to Daniel is asked.
Read by ledger_append in bin/lib/team.sh (through bin/lib/ledger.jq) and printed by team-log --help.

launch.about: request is the link to Daniel's Discord message, on an ops launch

closed.about: a legacy task's lists are empty; the hand-written legacy closes before strict_from have none

blocked.about: a worker stopped by an obstacle; the next launch or resumed clears it

waiting.about: a task parked on Daniel or something outside the team; the next launch or resumed clears it

resumed.about: clears held, blocked, paused and waiting

review.about: sent_back: the numbers of the notes sent back to the builder before the merge, each a correctness, security or real-data note; every other note became a follow-up

merge-approved.about: Daniel's word on the PR at url, one of the task's pr events; legacy lines name only the number

retro-schedule.about: Daniel's word on how often a retro runs, read by team-retro from the latest across the ledger; every_hours 0 stops the retros

stowed.about: one per open task at a handoff: worktrees as {project, branch, head}, with uncommitted: true for one whose changes the checkpoint kept as wip/<project>/T<n> on the team home's origin; roles whose sessions the handoff stopped

worktree-moved.about: team-open --resume, when this machine's worktree for the task in project is not the recorded one

injection.about: outside text that asked role to act: source is where it was (a URL, a path, a command, or <collection>/<_id>), text what it asked, never the personal details it held
